punchline: Get 1 percent better each day and you multiply to 37.78 in a year; get 1 percent worse and you're left with 0.03.
thirty_sec: James Clear does the math: 1 percent better every day for a year comes to about 37.78 times, and 1 percent worse comes to 0.03. A single day shows nothing, because results arrive late. He compares it to an ice cube in a room that warms from 25 to 26, 27, 28 degrees and doesn't change until 32. The calculation is an illustration, not a prediction.
